properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 5 at 1:37AM EDT until September 5 at 2:15AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
SVRIWX

The National Weather Service in Northern Indiana has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Lagrange County in northeastern Indiana...
St. Joseph County in southwestern Michigan...
Southwestern Branch County in southwestern Michigan...

* Until 215 AM EDT.

* At 137 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Centreville,
or near Sturgis, moving southeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Sturgis, Three Rivers, Centreville, Nottawa, Fawn River, Burr Oak,
Gilead, Brighton, Klinger Lake, Fishers Lake, Wasepi, Howe,
Findley, and Ontario.

This includes Interstate 80 in Indiana between mile markers 117 and
132.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 5 at 12:33AM CDT until September 5 at 1:30AM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
SVRBIS

The National Weather Service in Bismarck has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Burke County in northwestern North Dakota...

* Until 130 AM CDT.

* At 1233 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles south of
Lignite, or 34 miles east of Crosby, moving northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Bowbells, Lignite, Portal, Flaxton and Northgate.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 5 at 1:42AM EDT until September 5 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
At 142 AM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Fayette, or 9
miles southwest of Morenci, moving southeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Pioneer, Ransom, Betzer, and Alvordton.
properties.instruction:
A tornado watch remains in effect for the warned area. Tornadoes can
develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Although a tornado is not
immediately likely, if one is spotted act quickly and move to a place
of safety inside a sturdy structure, such as a basement or small
interior room.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 4 at 8:09PM CDT until September 6 at 10:36AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Jefferson,
Hardin, Jasper and Orange Counties.

Village Creek Near Kountze affecting Hardin County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Jefferson and Hardin
Counties.

For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Minor flooding is forecast.
For the Village Creek...including Kountze...Moderate flooding is
forecast.
For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Village Creek near Kountze.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 21.9 feet, At this level, water will be flowing over
the Highway 418 bridge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Friday the stage was 21.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM CDT Friday was 22.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 5.9 feet Wednesday
evening.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.8
feet on 02/12/1966.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 815 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 5 at 1:13AM EDT until September 5 at 5:15AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Cape May County in southern New Jersey...
Southeastern Cumberland County in southern New Jersey...

* Until 515 AM EDT.

* At 113 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 30
minutes. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Wildwood, Sea Isle City, Avalon, Stone Harbor, Goshen, Green
Creek, Cape May Court House, Eldora, Dennisville, Rio Grande and
Scotch Bonnet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
